schemes.label: Umsatzsteuer-Identifikationsnummer (USt-IdNr.)
schemes.helpText: German EU VAT number (DE + 9 digits) — needed to qualify as B2B for cross-border VAT treatment.

provenance.resolutionNote: Root TODO item 19 — this file was first added under item 16 with `appliesTo: 'COMPANY'` and no UStG text read at all (see this scheme's own git history). This task read §14 Abs. 4 UStG and §14a UStG directly at gesetze-im-internet.de (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ustg_1980/__14.html and .../__14a.html, fetched 2026-09-01) and can now quote the exact provisions: § 14 Abs. 4 Satz 1 Nr. 2 UStG — 'Eine Rechnung muss folgende Angaben enthalten: ... 2. die dem leistenden Unternehmer vom Finanzamt erteilte Steuernummer oder die ihm vom Bundeszentralamt für Steuern erteilte Umsatzsteuer-Identifikationsnummer'. § 14a Abs. 3 Satz 2 UStG (innergemeinschaftliche Lieferung) — 'In der Rechnung sind auch die Umsatzsteuer-Identifikationsnummer des Unternehmers und die des Leistungsempfängers anzugeben.' § 14a Abs. 1 Satz 3 UStG (grenzüberschreitende sonstige Leistung nach § 3a Abs. 2 mit Steuerschuldnerschaft des Leistungsempfängers im Ausland) states the identical sentence for that other cross-border case. `appliesTo` was changed from 'COMPANY' back to 'BOTH' (matching the removed compliance engine's own choice at git tag avant-refonte-documents, backend/src/compliance/profiles/data/de.ts) because § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 2 binds 'der leistende Unternehmer' — any business person issuing an invoice, whether organized as a company or as an individual registered/unregistered trader (Einzelunternehmer) — not companies specifically; German law does not gate this on legal form. `required` stays false for TWO independently sourced reasons, not one: (1) § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 2 itself offers Steuernummer OR Umsatzsteuer-Identifikationsnummer — either satisfies the law, so a USt-IdNr specifically is never itself a flat mandate, and this catalog has no separate 'Steuernummer' scheme (schema.ts's own header: 'LEGAL_ID' and 'VAT' are the only two schemes any shipped file uses today, a third would render with no dedicated data-cy) so a Steuernummer-holding, USt-IdNr-less business cannot be told apart from one that has neither; (2) § 14a's dual-VAT-number rule only fires for specific cross-border scenarios (intra-Community supply, or a cross-border B2B service under reverse charge), not every invoice, and a private consumer or a Kleinunternehmer (§19 UStG small-business exemption) has no USt-IdNr to give at all — the exact same 'no per-company VAT-regime input to condition on' reasoning `data/fr.json`'s own VAT entry in this same catalog already gives. What remains genuinely unsourced is the `pattern` itself: the DE + 9-digit format (ISO 7064 Mod 11,10 checksum) is well documented (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VAT_identification_number#Germany, cross-checked against this codebase's own `documents/tax/vat-syntax.ts#validateDeVat`, which cites the same Wikipedia page) but neither §14 nor §14a UStG states a format, and an attempt today (2026-09-01) to reach the issuing authority's own page (https://www.bzst.de/DE/Unternehmen/Identifikationsnummern/Umsatzsteuer_Identifikationsnummer/umsatzsteuer_identifikationsnummer_node.html) returned HTTP 404. Since schema.ts's own header treats `pattern` as a legal CLAIM covered by this fact's provenance exactly like `required`, and the pattern is the one piece not sourced to a primary/official text, the whole fact stays 'unverified' rather than being split — same all-or-nothing grading US EIN's entry in data/us.json already uses when a read text settles most, but not all, of a fact's claim. What would settle the pattern specifically: a BZSt or EU publication describing the USt-IdNr format directly.

schemes.label: Handelsregisternummer
schemes.helpText: Commercial register number (Amtsgericht + HRB/HRA, e.g. HRB 12345 München)

provenance.resolutionNote: New for root TODO item 19 — this scheme did not exist in the shipped file before (only inherited as a candidate from the removed compliance engine's own DE profile, git tag avant-refonte-documents, backend/src/compliance/profiles/data/de.ts's requiredIdentifiers: scheme LEGAL_ID, label Handelsregisternummer, appliesTo COMPANY, no pattern — that profile carried NO provenance field at all, so its choice was never sourced there either). This task read § 37a HGB directly at gesetze-im-internet.de (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/hgb/__37a.html, fetched 2026-09-01): 'Auf allen Geschäftsbriefen des Kaufmanns gleichviel welcher Form, die an einen bestimmten Empfänger gerichtet werden, müssen seine Firma, die Bezeichnung nach § 19 Abs. 1 Nr. 1, der Ort seiner Handelsniederlassung, das Registergericht und die Nummer, unter der die Firma in das Handelsregister eingetragen ist, angegeben werden.' (§ 37a Abs. 1 HGB). Two things this text does NOT settle, exactly the caution root TODO item 19 asked for: (1) it governs 'Geschäftsbriefe' (business letters/correspondence) addressed to a specific recipient — the word 'Rechnung' (invoice) never appears in § 37a HGB at all, so whether an invoice counts as a Geschäftsbrief for this purpose is an interpretive question this task did not chase down to a further primary source (case law or an official commentary would settle it — none was read); (2) § 37a HGB binds a 'Kaufmann' (a merchant registered in the Handelsregister — GmbH, AG, OHG, KG, eingetragener Kaufmann/e.K.), not every company: a company that never registered as a Kaufmann (e.g. a small GbR) has no Handelsregisternummer to give at all, which is the reasoning behind `required: false`. Corroborating evidence the number is NOT a tax-invoice-law requirement: § 14 Abs. 4 UStG's own exhaustive list of the ten mandatory invoice particulars (read in this same research pass, see this file's VAT entry above) does not mention a Handelsregisternummer anywhere. `appliesTo` stays 'COMPANY' as in the removed profile — an individual German Kaufmann (e.K.) could in principle also hold a Handelsregisternummer, but that nuance was not chased further here. What would settle this: case law or an official commentary establishing whether a Rechnung is a Geschäftsbrief under § 37a HGB, and whether an individually-registered Kaufmann (as opposed to a corporate form) should also carry this requirement in this catalog's `appliesTo`.
